description.narrative: The UNDP Environment and Climate Change Programme of the Samoa Multi-country office covers three countries, Cook Islands, Niue and Samoa, and the territory of Tokelau – and is defined as part of the the MCPD (2023-2027). The development challenges faced by Samoa, the Cook Islands, Niue, and Tokelau are multifaceted, with each territory grappling with its own unique combination of local, regional, and global issues under the Triple Planetary Crisis of climate change, biodiversity and nature loss, and pollution and waste, Despite their varying sizes, these small island nations share many common development obstacles, such as climate change, loss of biodiversity, limited economic diversification, dependence on remittances and external aid, and social inequality. The vision of the Cooperation Framework is that all people in the Pacific, leaving no one behind, are equal and free to exercise their fundamental rights, enjoy gender equality and peace, resilient to existential threats, and live in harmony with the blue continent. Towards this vision, this UNDP programme will contribute and provide leadership to one specific Cooperation Framework outcome area (‘Planet’), and will guide joint planning, monitoring, and reporting.The objectives of this programme gives UNDP Samoa MCO specific tools to support our Pacific Island Countries and Territories under the “Planet” main pillar of the MCPD in response to the Triple Planetary Crisis (1) in strengthening and implementing their nationally determined contributions under the Paris Agreement, with better analysis of the critical climate security challenges they face. This will include supporting multi-stakeholder decision-making processes as part of the Climate Promise 3.0, applying gender-responsive climate information for adaptation and mitigation, and helping partners manage the national greenhouse gas inventory, process, climate change measurement, reporting, and verification.
